title: Good app!
body:
I really like the app! I use the free version, so I’m not sure what I’m missing out on compared to the paid version, but it does everything I need it to do.

My only complaint is that there’s no way to correct your stats if you forget to reset your tracker. The last time I quit smoking, I eventually started again but didn’t reset my tracker until I quit again. Because of that, my stats say my longest streak was 273 days, when my actual longest streak is my current, 96 days.

It’s definitely not a big deal, but it gives me that tiny little twinge in my brain every time I see the incorrect number. 😆 I wish there were a way to manually correct it.

Other than that, I really enjoy the app. It’s fun and motivating to see how far you’ve come, and being able to look at my progress genuinely helps me keep pushing!

title: No complaints
body:
This app is perfect for what I wanted. I track 8 habits on it. I love that you can see stats and trends about each one. The inability to edit dates keeps you honest. 

I also find the widgets very valuable. I keep one on my homepage but I really love the one you can put on your lock screen. I see it every time I open my phone. It’s a good reminder. You can also set goals and reminders but I haven’t done that yet.

I do not understand being upset you have to pay for some features. Do you think they developed this app for $0? And seriously, I pay $12 a year. That’s $1 a month. It’s more than worth it. Get a grip. 

Honestly I think this app has helped me avoid relapsing several times.

title: I’m not one to spend time writing a review but this is an Incredible App!!
body:
I use Days Since for everything. I track bad habits like excessive social media use and picking at my skin. But I also use it for things like tracking when I last washed my bedsheets, got my oil changed, rotated my tires, cleaned the bathroom, etc. 

Lots of apps require you to sign up, make an account, agree to a free trial, or endure dozens of spam emails. Days Since does not, you don’t need to click the little X on pop up ads when you open the app, because there isn’t any. And you’re never asked to spend money or “upgrade.” Fantastic app.

title: Love the app but….
body:
I really like this app overall. I recently downloaded it to track how many days I’ve been away from social media. Most of the other apps I found are focused on sobriety or addiction recovery, whereas this app feels much more general purpose and can be used for many different goals.

My biggest issue is that the iOS widget is locked behind a subscription. A basic widget that simply lets you glance at your streak without opening the app feels like a core feature rather than a premium one.

I also feel that the frequent prompts to upgrade to the paid version are a bit discouraging. Instead of putting the widget behind the paywall, I’d rather see cosmetic features, such as custom app icons, reserved for the premium version. That would still provide value for subscribers while making the free version more practical for everyday use.

Overall, it’s a well designed app with a lot of potential, but making the basic widget free would significantly improve the experience.

title: Days Since Habit Tracker App
body: I have thoroughly enjoyed using the days since app to track my habits that I wanted so badly to change and I have successfully reached 298 days. And the entire 298 days I have used this app to track it. I want to be honest with my review and so that means I have to state the issues with the app and honestly the only issue I have come across is that it’s so easy somehow to reset the counter through the widget. I have reset my counter several times on accident somehow. The first time I done it I was so disappointed and upset but then I learned how to take away the reset thankfully. I have worked so hard on my habit that when I first reset it I was truly devastated but now that I know how to fix the issue it’s been fine. I would just ask if there is a way to not have the reset function so easily accessible or able to be done on accident. If there was like a confirmation question or something that would be helpful because then it’s a lot less likely to accidentally hit the correct buttons more than once in a row. But other than the one issue I have ran into the app has been amazing. I do think at times that the app should somehow give motivational quotes or some type of support to the customer and not just have it only to track the time. It would be a lot more enticing to people if it offered some type of support or interaction.

title: 17 dollars for a widget is stupid
body: Genuinely one of the worst subscription prices for what it offers. All you get is a widget that shows you the tracking information. You can literally get a day counter app and just reset it whenever you relapse for free. This is a horrible price for such a small feature. Maybe if it was around 2-5 dollars this would be a good price. The amount of developing it takes to create something like this is so small and lazy. All you need is a day counter which is easy to code, a widget design which is easy to add, and something to reset it. that’s it. Whoever programmed this app probably didn’t even need 17 dollars to create the small amount of code needed for this. It’s absurd and you shouldn’t support these greedy developers taking advantage of addicts.

title: An end to addictions
body:
Because of this app alone, I can say I have not been on Instagram/TikTok for 523 days, after previously spending hours and hours a day wasting my life to doomscrolling.

The reason this app works is that each counter is a commitment to yourself to a goal, and a personal challenge to hit a certain number of days. In seeing a tangible number (easily visible as a widget on your phone), it helps to remind you of your end goal. As that number grows, you become more and more empowered to keep going. 

I love this app for its simplicity and effectiveness in ending bad habits. I would recommend it to anyone.

title: I use this to track literally everything
body:
As someone with ADHD, I find this app to be a game changer to keep up with life admin, cleaning, and anything that happens on a periodic schedule. While it was designed to help quit habits like smoking, I find it to be incredibly useful for maintaining good habits as well. 

The biggest difference for me with this app vs other ones used for managing schedules is the lack of notifications. I love that this app doesn’t nag me. It takes a completely neutral stance on the length of the streak. If I want to do laundry 2x a week, other apps, trackers,  or calendars end up reminding you to do that task on a specific day. If I don’t feel like it that day, I clear the event/notification because it’s annoying and then I completely forget about it. With days since, I can log in on my own schedule, and see it’s been 4 days since I’ve done laundry so I should get to that soon. I mostly login once a day to updatea trying I did that day and scroll through my long list of things I’m tracking to see if anything stands out that I should focus on. 

Here’s some example things I track: 
-changed the air filter 
-took dog to vet
-got a haircut 
-worked out 
-vacuumed the living room
-purchased on Amazon 
-did laundry
-got an oil change 
-went to the doctor
-drank alcohol
-registered car at the dmv 
-refilled my meds
-went out to eat
-worked on a hobby 
-took a vacation

I probably track 100+ things at this point, and anytime I do something that I rarely do, like wash the curtains, I’ll add that to the tracker as well. 

P.S. I got the paid version for better colors. It’s not necessary but the base colors were way too bright for me, and I don’t mind supporting the devs since I use this app so much.

title: Helps me quit bad habits and start good ones!
body: I have been trying to quit bad habits that don’t serve me well in my life for two or three years now. I’ve gone through many apps in an attempt to help. I get excited about the app and then a few weeks after I fall short and the app doesn’t do anything for me once I’ve slipped backwards into my old self. This app is truly a game changer for me though. It’s such an easy and user-friendly interface and I can put multiple habits and see them all as soon as I open the app. I want to quit smoking, so I can see how many days since I’ve last smoked. But I also want to start exercising and stretching more. So I can see the days since I’ve lasted exercised and stretched. And it has helped me develop good habits as well as quit the bad ones. And when I do good things I’m excited to go and reset the calendar and see that I’ve been exercising every day! I’ve been recommending it to friends and it is just so easy and no pressure. Love it and I’ve been using it now for the past 3 months, I love checking in on it frequently :)

title: A Simple App That Actually Helps You Grow
body:
I use this app to track my sobriety, and it’s genuinely made my life easier. It takes some of the pressure off my already stressful days, and I love opening it up to see my progress. While so many apps feed unhealthy habits or promote toxic lifestyles, this one does the opposite — it’s simple, supportive, and genuinely useful.

I’d give it a 10/10 for anyone wanting to stay mindful of their habits — whether you’re quitting drinking, smoking, resisting the urge to text your ex, or just keeping tabs on your fitness, diet, workload, or even travel deadlines. Whatever your goal, Days Since helps you stay accountable in the best way.

title: Simply an Exceptional Productivity Tool
body:
I discovered this app and immediately found it to be a great tool for tracking life events, chores, and the little daily things that I want to remember the last time something occurred.

I joined the Count Up Club Subscription, which immediately unlocked the full potential of this tool.

This app lives in my iPhone dock, and I use it multiple times per day.

Pros: Simple, lightweight, beautifully designed, many customization options in terms of colors. It's basically an app that lets choose a name, time, and date (along with color-coded tiles) for whatever kind of event you create, which the app keeps track of for you.

Suggestions for Improvement: Custom layout options for tiles (examples: 3x3 scrolling grid of tiles on iPhone, list view for streaks). Ability to add context to individual streak items, such as a notes section that can be accessed and edited on the fly. Expand the calendar functionality to add streak starts and resets to sync with Apple Calendar/ Google Calendar. Add fun and rewarding customizable animations when adding/resetting streak counters. Rework the time and interface when adding/resetting streaks to utilize more screen area (larger and easier to adjust).

I love your application, and I see the potential to make it even better! For users like me who use it for multiple productivity tracking uses, this app is a game changer! Thank you to the small team Ivo, Nadya, Stan, Petar, for bringing such a useful tool to life. Let's make some improvements! You all rock!

title: Love it… But one request!
body: I love this app and I especially like how you can see the data broken down by number of resets, longest streak, etc. as well as the ability to set goals. If I could make one request it would be for an addition function to have the ability to manually click to add to a tally. For example, I ride mountain bikes and sometimes I’ll set a goal to ride a certain number of times within a week or a month. I’ve had my fair share of injuries from riding as well so that requires ongoing maintenance  exercises. I have a habit of slowly trailing off and not doing those exercises. If I could set a goal of, say, 3 days a week, being able to check those off manually and tracking it would be a great addition to the goal setting section. I have tried other apps for that stuff but they’re not great. This app is perfect and if I could also do this all in one place I’d have no problem paying again as an add on feature. The only way for me to track that in this app now is to do it backwards. Where a reset is a good thing but that gets confusing!  Anyway. Keep up the great work and hopefully I’ll see that extra function available soon!!!

title: Helps me moderate and to never forget
body:
My childhood dog died this year. He was 14. He was my world. He was a brother. He was there for me when no one else was. He taught me things I didn’t think a dog would do. I never took him for granted. I knew one day that that day would happen and it broke me. So I put his death in so I don’t forget about him, because sometimes when I’m on my low, I think about him and I think what he’s done to me and it helps me think straight to move forward. 

I’ve also been monitoring my cannabis intake recently. I used to do it every day and once I realized I was just smoking just to smoke, I knew I had to moderate and stop. I went cold turkey for about two weeks and just reevaluated my relationship with cannabis and overall lifestyle, I’m eating healthier, working out more, and figuring out what I wanna do with my life. (Ironically I wanna be cop, and try out for SWAT.) But I’m more mindful of what I’m doing now and have set clear goals for myself which I haven’t done in very long time.

RIP SPIKEY

title: Genuine
body:
When trying to quit anything- especially an addiction- programs meant to ‘help’ you are so often scams that prey on addicts.  It’s so depressing to see so many apps or other programs like this one which are subscription based, utilize frustrating amounts of forced ads, or make you pay in some other way, which ultimately all depend on you failing your goals to make money.  This app is not like that and feels genuine; you can track, as far as I know, a few ‘habits’ pretty much infinitely and every necessary feature in that tracking is free.  There are some paid options to have notifications or whatever, but nothing necessary is blocked and you are not punished at all for having to reset, which makes it easier to be honest if I relapse.  This is important to me and something so many other apps miss.  If I relapse I already feel bad and the app punishing me for it too would just make me feel worse, so I like how neutral this app remains on resetting a streak but still keeping track of resets.  It’s very useful both for myself and my therapist in tracking addictions and bad habits, and in noticing patterns.  I’ve been using this app for over a year now and it’s nice to see some numbers and streaks grow.

On the note of neutrality, though, I think it would be nice if there were options to reach certain milestones- I’d like to have the choice to feel some sort of gratification beyond the number when I’ve reached, say, 100 days without breaking a streak.  Maybe even just a little congratulation message or something you can configure, or even the font of the number changing to something fancier, like, “look, you’ve made it to the big numbers now.”

Otherwise the app does what it needs to for me, without feeling like the developers want me to fail to pay them more, which I can appreciate.  I also like some of the smaller features, like that it can be a widget, though you have to pay to use that part fully, but it’s helpful as a reminder.  I appreciate having the choice to lock the app so other people can’t go in my business, and the configurability of the tracker with custom naming and colors means it can be used to track anything really.  The calender is a nice touch to see when and how often I break certain streaks and to notice patterns- like that I apparently tend to relapse more often on mondays and fridays! The design is simple; on one hand, it isn’t overdone or overly cheery, which makes navigating the app easy and doesn’t seem fake or annoying.  On the down side the utilitarian-style sometimes makes me wish I could edit or play with the colors, fonts, or background of the app since I use it so often, to make it more “my space.”

All in all a good app and does what you want it to, with paid features that I’m sure are nice but are not necessary which makes it accessible to the people who need it most.  And, like I mentioned in the title, its intentions feel genuine- which can be hard to find these days.

title: Love this app!
body:
I truly love this app, it’s been such a valuable tool for me in many ways. I first started using it to track my sobriety (which is great because I don’t want to consciously count the days myself, but having Days Since counting in the background always gives me an exact reference of where I’m at) and as of this review I know I am on Day 357! 🙏 ~ Days Since has also been a game-changer with tracking my retention streaks breaking free of PMO- the reset feature in particular is super helpful and effective in this situation because it tracks every reset down to the days and hours, so you can always go back and see all the months retaining with all the setbacks in between ~ And now I am also using Days Since to track my medications so I always know exactly how long I’ve been taking them and when I started.

So many uses and my favorite thing of all is that I’m able to use the features I need (especially the widgets) without hitting a paywall <3

I actually never write reviews (this is probably my first ever) but this app has been so great that when a screen popped up asking me to write a review I was more than happy to do so. It’s the least I can do for all the value these devs have provided me through this tool. 10/10 must download for tracking days on anything!

title: A Quiet Companion That’s Meant Everything
body:
It’s hard to put into words what the Days Since app has meant to me over the past two years. When I made the decision to get sober, I didn’t know what the road ahead would look like. I just knew I needed something — anything — to help me take it one day at a time. This app became that something.

It’s simple, honest, and quietly powerful. No pressure, no judgment — just a space to mark each sober day and see how far I’ve come. Some days I opened it with pride. Other days, I opened it just to remind myself that I could keep going. It helped me stay connected to my progress when everything else felt overwhelming.

Days Since may look like just a counter, but for me, it’s been a symbol of strength, resilience, and hope. Two years later, I’m still here. And that little number growing day by day has played a bigger role in that than I ever expected. I’m deeply grateful.

title: Simple and Effective!!
body:

I track things like the last time I drank, cried, clipped my chihuahuas nails, or even washed my sheets—and having those visual reminders helps me stay mindful of my habits and patterns.

What I love most is how it helps me break bad habits and celebrate progress without judgment. Watching the numbers go up feels like a small win each day, and when I reset one, it gives me a chance to reflect and refocus. Whether you’re working on goals, mental health, or just trying to be more consistent with everyday tasks, this app is surprisingly powerful. Highly recommend it for anyone on a self-improvement journey!

title: Does what it says but can be better
body:
If you want to track time for a habit or something else, this one is great. For the free version you can add multiple timers (is actually a stopwatch displayed in hours, days, weeks, months, years) but if you want to set a goal (amongst other features) you need to pay ($20 a year is reasonable)

This is what I wish the app would do as well: 

- Have a count on something since I started the timer (click every time it happens) 

- Have also an actual timer (not stopwatch) with a fixed amount of time that counts down to zero. This would be great combined with the previous point if I want to track how many times something happened during a fixed time.

- Pause timer and restart it without deleting the timer. I like to see how long I fast (in hrs) When I’m done I don’t need the time to keep running so I delete the timer and make another one on the next fast. If I could pause and reset, I could see how many times and for how long on average I’ve fasted since I created the timer.

Overall great experience, I have the free version and no annoying ads or anything in the app, with those extra features it would be better but it still does what it says perfectly.

title: Used to be a favorite app, but the constant nagging to subscribe is downer
body:
Update March 2025: They STILL don’t offer a way to turn off the spammy nag popups. 

Update: Lowered to one star based on dev’s tone deaf response. Again, I would have been happy to pay a reasonable amount (Not $50 for “lifetime access”) And the dev’s reply didn’t even address the simplest and easiest thing they could do - turn off the constant nagging to upgrade. 

Original review:
I don’t mind paying for good software at all, and believe in supporting indie developers who make good stuff. This app really scratches a crucial itch: A no-nonsense, flexible way of tracking multiple counters over time. I’d happily pay a one-time fee to turn off the constant nagging to join the new “Premium Club.” 

Unfortunately, not only are the new enhancements like Siri integration and data portability (which frankly shouldn’t be a “premium” feature) locked behind a subscription, but the app keeps periodically interrupting you with a pitch to subscribe, with no option to say “Nope, I won’t ever subscribe.”) Effectively meaning that being “non-premium” is actually a significant downgrade. In fact, almost none of the premium features require any kind of ongoing, server-side service. I’d love to take advantage of the new Shortcuts integration, for example. 

And again, I’d be happy to pay for the upgrade! I’m not saying the app should be free. But this whole trend of turning device-side features into “subscriptions”, regardless of whether there’s actually any SaaS component of any kind, is really unfortunate. And it’s a shame to see another great app get swept up in it, without even an option to say “Could you at least stop nagging me and let me keep using the hobbled version I was already happy with?”

People with ADHD often struggle with something called time blindness, and this app helps me keep track of time since I’ve done important tasks so that I don’t accidentally go weeks without keeping up with household chores. title: Five Stars for Basic Habit Tracking
body:
This app is great for basic habit tracking, to help you quit whatever. I gave it four stars because the process for adding reminders is a bit awkward, and the subscription fee seems high for an app that doesn’t have a lot of reporting capabilities. The ability to add a note on a reset event is great, but a way to identify relapse patterns would be awesome.

I’m using the app to track one habit I want to quit, and a couple habits I want to enforce. I avoid cardio, but really need to do it, so I’m using the app in reverse, to show me the last time I did cardio. I have it send daily reminders and when I do cardio, I click reset, and the clock starts counting up again. When the reminder says, “congrats, you haven’t done cardio in a day,” I take it as a sarcastic reminder.

Dear Developer, if you don’t have an app for habit encouragement tracking…

update: i am changing my rating from a 5 star to 4 star. maybe i’m being picky but i really don’t like how in the more recent UI updstes, when i view my resets, i can only see the first 5 or 6, its as if the font is waaaay larger. it doesn’t allow me to have a good visual understanding of how many resets ive had and how frequently if i can only see a few at a time. maybe a setting where we can adjust the font size so that we can see more?

great app, helped me quit nicotine. it would be nice to add a feature that tells you the total amount of time you were free. i.e. if i had to reset 3x in a month, it would be good to see the total amount of days i was “alcohol free”. so it might say “28/31 days alcohol free this month” or “320/365 days alcohol free this year”. great app otherwise

title: Simple and Reliable
body:
I love this app and how I can keep track of my habits, good or bad. Everything is color coded and you can sort by day, week, months, etc. No login or signup required either.

It would be cool if there was a separate counter that you could edit so you can keep track of variable tasks that aren't done every day. The option to pause a counter would be helpful too for breaks or interruptions in the patterns of some habits I track. 

Also highly appreciate the way the development team treats its users. I never write reviews but I like the way they asked and their reasoning. I miss simple and straightforward apps like these it's a real throwback to the original apps that were developed for smartphones in the early 2010s.

title: Really helpful!
body: I got this app, along with the “I am Sober” app. I’m currently working on quitting a couple addictions, so I thought being held accountable would be very helpful. I really love how you’re able to add multiple addictions. The “I am Sober” app only allows for 2 addictions (without paying), but I had 3 that I wanted to work on. So, I was able to add all three to this app, and it’s been great! It’s a pretty simple app, so it’s perfect if you’re just simply using it to track your sober streak. However, there aren’t as many features as the “I am Sober” app offers. This being said, a lot of the extra features on that app are only for “premium” members anyway. Though this app has some features you need to pay for, it is a great deal for $17.99 a YEAR! Overall I’d give it a 9/10!

Since we are both on several now and they can be 30, 60 or 90 day supplies, and few seem to be on the same pick up schedule, this helps me know when they are due. Maybe there are better uses but this has been extremely helpful for me tracking renewals and refills.

title: 3 years in and I have some thoughts
body:
i have been using this app for a little over 3 years, and honestly it has prevented me from acting impulsively, but i have a few ideas to make it more effective. 
1) maybe if you make the markers more personalized it would add more emotional connection? like maybe the background could be a photograph from someone’s camera roll? 
2) i don’t want to pay to have people see my progress, (i think it is free to share?), but maybe if you had something free that made it so you can share with one person for a 30 day period? 
((maybe after that period ended it would incentivize people to purchase the entire package.))
3) add something where people can journal their thoughts that day. if they are having a hard time they could open the app, not only see their progress, but also write down their either positive or negative thoughts. it keeps track of progress and lengthens time spent on the app. 

the last thing i want to say is i am NOT a computer person. i don’t get technology i struggle immensely with basic stuff, but this app is easy for me to use. the only difficulty i would say is sometimes i get lost navigating and it might be too easy to delete or reset, bc ive been close and accidentally reset or deleted my icons and it was obviously disappointing. 

anyway, my name is lauren and im just a random girl in college with clearly not a lot else on her plate LOL thank you for creating the app!! have a good rest of your day

It's nice for getting a quick view of all your habits and reflecting on your current state in relation to how long it's been. I managed to quit using reddit thanks to this app (at least for 450 hours as of now).
 
For bad habits, you try to get the number as high as you can. I also find it useful for seeing how long since i drank alcohol, for example, and reflecting on how I feel after a certain amount of time.

For good habits, the goal is to keep the "hours since" as close to zero as possible. For example, to track how long since you called your parents, meditated, etc.

One idea for improvement would be allowing the user to flag good/bad habits, or to set a goal to not go over a certain amount of time for these good habits.

It would also be nice to change the time of entry and view historical entries from the watch app, since right now i need to pull out my phone to do this.

title: Easy to use for tracking anything!

Before days since it seemed like we were in a constant state of colds, coughs, and fevers. One kid starts to feel better then another one seems to be coming down with something. Little Petri dishes really lol. And eventually the adults are sick too. Vicious cycle. Anyways, I started using days since to track our colds and have a better idea of who patient zero was, who needs to quarantine, and who’s been healthy. It really changed our understanding of everything and we started making some changes to improve our health: showers immediata after school. Hand sanitizer in backpacks. Better room cleaning consistency. Now with this insight we’re way less sick! I haven’t been sick for 100 days today, my last longest stretch was 65 days. The kids have good streaks going too. Anyways, a little extra attention with the help of our days since tracker and you can do a lot of good for yourself and your family. Cheers!

- As a timer for life events: “How many months since I started my job”
- As a duration timer. “How long have I been eating keto”

For the first two, it’s stellar. The the last one, it works well, but I’d like to be able to pause if I decide to quit eating keto and come back to it later to record again. Then I could make better use of the calendar. 

Either way, this app is far and away the best of its class, and the generic branding makes it applicable for many scenarios. Nice work.

title: I’m In Love With This App!!
body:
Let me tell you why this app is SO great! 

I’m a personal trainer and needing to stay consistent with my goals & helping others stay consistent with their goals is 90% of the job! 

This app is great because it’s an automatic tracker to let you know how consistent you’ve been with said goal you are working on!

And it’s better than just crossing things off on a calendar in my opinion… and I’ll tell you why.

It eliminate that extra step off needing to tick each day whether you have stuck to your goals that day or not! Because it’s always tracking! 

You ONLY have to re-update it when you fell off! 

And when it comes to sticking to a goal, anything that’s going to make achieving that goal take less steps is HUGE! 

Not only that since it’s always tracking, and you can add it as a widget to your home screen… you always have an accurate update of how many days you’ve been consistent with the habit! 

And since it’s on your phone it’s always super easy to show off to others as well! 

Doesn’t sound like a big deal, but when you’ve hit a big milestone like X amount of days no alcohol, for me I think over 90 days no Caffeine! And over 450 practicing Spanish!! It’s so nice to be able to physically show someone your hard work! 

And I’m not done yet haha, it’s so nice free you are to set your own goal.

I stress this all the time in my practice, but it’s the goal you can stick to that’s the goal you should start with and then progressively work your way to a “harder” goal.

So if 5 days a week of working out is too much, you can easily plug into this app something more manageable such as 1 day a week!

It sounds small but other apps aren’t always the best at this, and it really makes a difference because everyone’s goals are truly different. 

Last thing, but there’s so much science behind daily hitting a goal for yourself! 

Something about it… I’ve heard… (Andrew Huberman) helps to realize dopamine everyday. Your body loves to see you daily win the day… something like that.

And after listening to the podcast, knowing I had a couple bad habits myself (I overdo caffeine, over my daily limit) I STARTED WITH THIS APP!! 

And it was actually a really big turn around point in my life! 

Because every other time I tried to start a new habit, I’d do good at staying consistent. 

But with the extra hard habits that I was really struggling to stick to. Having that extra layer of knowing how many days in I am was the extra push I needed to keep going.

Even if it was only 1 day, day 1 was always the hardest and after that seeing myself stick to the hard goals for 2..3..4..10..15 days really really motivated me to keep going.

I CANT stress it enough I’m IN LOVE WITH THIS APP!! 

I think everyone should have it!!

body:
I don't use Days Since to track “bad” habit avoidance streaks. I use it to keep track of when winter/summer solstice was and the equinoxes. I use it to see how long since certain car maintenance was performed. I use it to see how long since I last washed my hair. Etc, etc.

So it’s useful for positive habits and just points of curiosity, too. For example I’m writing this 45 days after the summer solstice and the weather is starting to shift. Very interesting!

Excellent app with clean simple style. Much appreciated.

title: most useful app on my phone!! 5/5
body:
I use this app for a different use than what the developers had in mind most likely, but its been super helpful either way! Ive been using this app to track some medications and when
¡ last ate, similar things like that. Its been super helpful to be able to open the app and be able to figure out when i last did things so i dont take my meds to early or go to long without eating! Its probably my most often opened app on my phone and by FAR the most helpful! The reset button is very simple and i LOVE LOVE LOVE that you can adjust the time you reset it, delete resets, and my favorite feature is being able to add notes!!! its also super helpful that it averages out the time between resets, counts how many resets, longest streak, and how long its been since the little counter was created at the bottom!! its super easy to organize, name, and color each little timer thing!! its really helpful that you can choose how to order the counters, especially since there is a custom option!! the only issue i have is a very small one, the fact that there are limited colors and you cant set reminders if you dont pay, but i totally understand the need to make money (especially since it is ad free!!!) and they arent super important features, just little extra things. easily the most useful app on my phone, ive recommended it to a few friends!!!
10/10 easily!

title: It is really helping me, I just wish it had some more features.
body:
I’m 20. I’m trying to break and build a lot of habits right now, and this app is really helping me to keep it top of mind and progress forward.

I really wish it had three features that would help me in my journey:

1. when I’m resetting a counter, I’d like to be able to reset it by taking down the pure number of days rather than just writing in a reset date, which requires knowing the last reset date (it’s written there but, still easier to work by number directly). 
2. Id also like to be able to put a reset date before the previous one, allowing me to extend the counter (maybe I misplaced the previous one or want to count more days towards my goal)
3. Id like to be able to add a goal amount to the counters so they show a progress percentage that slowly goes up and maybe notifies me every day.
4. Id like line graphs and other useful data representations of my counters to help me visually and intuitively see my progress towards building (or here especially) beating a habit).

I’m now at 1394 days of zero nicotine and although I don’t check it as much anymore, I still open it every once in a while. title: Great for trying to quit skin picking or any other bad habits
body: This app is simple, has good widgets, and makes it easy to keep yourself accountable. I also really like that you can see your average streak, add descriptions to each reset, and look at your history of resets. this makes it really easy to review my progress and see how I’ve been improving overall, which is a huge morale boost. Also, I can see the severity of each reset through the descriptions, where I note if the picking wasn’t bad, moderate, or bad, how I felt afterwards, and where the picking was, which is also a huge part of the progress for me. I also really like how you can switch from the time frame you view it from between days, hours, weeks, months, years, etc. When I was having a lot of trouble not resetting multiple times a day, being able to see a non-zero number of hours instead of zero days helped a lot in getting over that initial hurdle of the first day or two. Only kind of negative thing is that I wish you could share the descriptions with each reset instead of just the length of time! I keep my boyfriend updated as he’s been supporting me with this, so to send resets to him I just take a screenshot of it open with its description instead of using the share button, which isn’t a big deal at all but just a tiny liiiiittle bit annoying. I wouldn’t want to share it without the context of the description, y'know? At least for what I’m using the app for. Something I would recommend for others if just having a counter isn’t motivating enough for quitting whatever you’re trying to is a brownie point system! For each extra day you’re able to resist, assign a reward point amount that increases the longer you go (going from earning 1 pt a day at 1 day to earning 3 pts a day at day 10) (I especially found that what works best for me is having the points being rewarded when I resist for 1 day, then 2 more days (day 3), then 3 more days (day 6), etc.) Then, you can have a menu of rewards that you have to spend points on — this especially works well if you make it so you can’t indulge in the rewards unless you spend points on it. You can set this up with a close friend, partner, family member, or yourself to offer rewards, and the sky is the limit. For me, this makes it so that instead of just losing this arbitrary number if I pick my skin, I actively have to choose between picking in that moment or a certain tangible reward, like a surprise from my boyfriend, a new book buy, or crumbl cookie. That’s a lot more motivating for me, and I’m able to maintain longer streaks, which feels spectacular.

title: It helps me
body:
I want to start this by saying this is my first review and that the app did ask me to write. 

Although this is the case, the app has really helped me. I have had server problems with bitting my lips and cheeks. This caused my jaw more pain. I have jaw problems, maybe because of the bitting, but I do believe that I would still have problems even if I didn’t have bitting issues. I do believe stopping the bitting has helped my jaw from hurting as much as it has. I still have problems but not as severe as it was.

For my cheek and lip bitting, I have two different timers. In the very beginning I had one. Then I got better at my cheek bitting and my lip bitting got worse so I made a new one. So far I have 5 timers. 

The other three timers are for negative thoughts and for when I go into my moods I have with my parents. 

At times I forget to restart the timer but that’s a problem with me forgetting or not being able to be on my phone. 

I have looked at the reasons to go premium but I do not find them appealing to me that I would like them. 

I do believe in the future I will pay, for the fact that I really do like this app and would like to support it. :))

title: Nice, does what it says
body: I like the app, did a trial and subscribed with the discounted yearly fee. The security settings are nice, so only I can access my content.   I like the reminders, but it uses the same generic phrase repeatedly. It would be nice to seem in an update making the reminders more varied and/or related to the set habit I am tracking. For instance, if I have to do a reset on a habit, my next reminder will say “Great job keep it up!” Even though it might only have been a couple hours past. And not a great job, because I just hit reset, LOL. So maybe work in some inspirational quotations or reflect the amount of time that’s gone by. If it’s been 6 months, the reminder ought to be like “Wow, 6 months is amazing! Feel good about that and keep up the good work, let’s keep it going another 6 months!”, instead of “Great job keep it up” for the 1,000th time.

title: Reinforce Your Change In Perspective
body:
I tend to jump to start (or in this case stop) some new thing, be it a project or habit or a change in attitude. I don’t really yet have the organizational skills to make some of these things a reality. But when I’m  looking to stop a destructive behavior, when life becomes more nightmare than dream, resources like this are invaluable to me. There’s other work to be done about those behaviors, obviously. But it’s super reassuring, no matter how badly I’m feeling, to be able to open up this app and see that I’ve made some kind of progress. It also keeps me honest when I’ve stopped that progress. 

It’s a really nicely put together app. Nice colors and fairly intuitive to use. You can track many things simultaneously and I’ve made use of that ability. 

Highly recommended by this user.

title: one major flaw
body:
loving the functionality and design of this app. paid for the pro version, and then discovered one major annoyance that almost made me delete the app entirely. it's the "reset" button on the widget, it is too easy to accidentally hit. i would appreciate if that button would prompt a pop up that clarifies, are you sure you want to reset your streak? 

this wouldn't be an issue if i could go in and either undo a reset, edit a reset, or change the time on the counter. since i cannot, if i accidentally hit the reset circle on the widget, i have to delete the counter and create a new one to accurately reflect my "days since". 

the home screen widget is the main point and purpose of this app for me, so the reset button is almost a deal breaker. maybe we could have the option to toggle the reset button on/off for the widget? 

love the app, can't wait to see these improvements, thanks 🙏

title: I wish I could Archive Events
body:
The app is good. It is simple to use, has friendly interface, and it does what it promises. But it lacks a few features that would make it so much better such as archiving events and adding a countdown feature for future events.

I use this app to track the time of important events in my life, and one of them is the my mom passed away. I still want to remember that day and track it because it is important to me, but I don’t necessarily want to have to look at it every single time I open the app. So I really wish there was an option to archive or “hide” some events to only open them in times we want to remember the date or reminisce about that specific event.

i’ve been struggling with sewerslide ideation since eight grade. with multiple attempts and countless self harm scars, i am still fighting for my life. i’ve used this app to track days without self harm for 147 days. i’ve had to reset it twice.***

So I use this app to track how long I have been clean of physical self-harm(4 years, coming up on 5) and how long it has been since my last suicide attempt(2 years), and every time I check this app and see those number go higher and higher gives me an unbelievable sense of pride that I have made it this far. title: Counting my habits without feeling ashamed when I restart
body:
I have been trying to establish more intentional habits since COVID turned me into a screen junky. I kept looking for apps for a Rule of Life but got things that measured physical spaces, and I searched for habit trackers and I had to interact with them so much it became just another reason to pick up my phone. I wanted something on my phone that would be the first thing I saw on the screen and also would remind me of my goals and my progress. 

This app does that very well with its widget feature. It’s right on my home screen counting away. At night if I miss my goal on something I restart the counter before I go to bed. I know which of my habits are easier to maintain and which ones need work. I’m pretty happy.

title: Way more than that thought it would be
body:
At first I downloaded because I wanted to have a counter available to view days since smoked. (I’m on day 66 now, yay).  Then I saw that I can have the banner show on my Lock Screen AND I can set alarms and shortcuts. 

I’m on a Social media “cleanse” and seeing that it’s only been 5 days makes me feel bad for wanting to log back in. That fact is just making me double down on staying off. 

In addition to showing your streaks, I can also work to keep the number of days in between “good” events low. 

I have a counter for days since called my mom, dad, brother, nephew- etc. I just called my dad (on what feels like yesterday) and it already says 14 days! Sorry dad.

Last week I added one for days since last been to the gym and today I updated it after 5 days. Felt good. 

Talk about a new way to hold yourself accountable and getting your priorities straight.

title: A gem
body: Honestly, this app is just perfect. It does one thing extremely well. I'm always amazed when people complain about an app being too simple. It's just an elegant design and it achieves everything it needs to achieve. And 11 bucks a year or whatever it is seems reasonable for that. It’s a really helpful app. That said, there are a couple ways in which I think the app could be improved. I have one broad feature in mind and one specific feature in mind. Firstly, it would be nice to have some more statistics or visualizations or insight into how you're doing versus the past. Are your relapses getting further and further apart, or are they coming closer together? Just some insight into how this compares to your best ever trend. Maybe resets per month, stuff like that. The second thing is much more simple and concrete. Basically, it would be nice to be able to edit the units without just selecting one. There's an app called Countdown that does this really nicely. You can select each unit independently of the others. So it has every unit from years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, and seconds. You know, I might have that slightly wrong, but it's roughly along those lines. And for each unit, you can tick whether to include it or not. In practice, I don't think that people often want to skip a bunch of units. Like, nobody's going to do years and seconds. But it's actually really nice for the widgets. In the app, I think you guys do a great job. For the widget, it would be nice for people who are trying to quit something right at the beginning and they're proud of just getting 5, 10, 15 minutes. But let's say you're trying to not interrupt someone and you're in a meeting. I mean, you might be proud of 20 minutes, but the lowest unit you have is hours. So I think it would just give you guys more flexibility if you keep the app exactly the same. But for the widgets, let people choose how to format the duration string and specifically what units to include. Anyway, thank you for building such a fantastic product. And I really appreciate the time and effort and attention to detail that you put into this product.

body:
I've been lucky and fortunate not to have any chemical addictions in my life, despite having grown up in a first-gen Irish Catholic family (which did not escape that scourge). 

However each Sunday after Mass I spent my weekly chores allowance on a big bag of Nestlé Crunch. Devouring it was transporting. Chocolate became a lifelong almost-daily habit, one that has not served me.

Because I have RLS, the immoderate amounts of sugar and caffeine have contributed to chronic sleep deprivation, which has led to all manner of sadnesses. 

What works for me, with the help of the "Days Since" app, is limiting myself to *up to two squares* only of top-quality chocolate per day. A better life has ensued. 

Also I tend to obsess about family and relationships, and this app is a simple way to keep me give me strokes for going days and weeks without doing so. Gamification works!

This simple app has let me calm my monkey-mind chatter around these common struggles by easily exporting them from my brain to my phone. 

It's also helped with a lesser problem that can get out of hand (so to speak): what the app euphemistically calls "fap". You know, rubbin' the nubbin, or chokin' the chicken.  

So thank you, devs.

title: From hopeless to hopeful
body: I struggle with a gambling addiction. Days Since has helped me manage daily my urges by giving me a new number to count besides money. It provides a similar dopamine spike to gambling and encourages me to keep going strong by giving me accomplishments to be proud of. I had a couple of resets at the beginning, but seeing the time gaps helped me identify what my triggers were throughout the day and how to preempt them. Whenever I have the urge to gamble I open the app and take a look at my current progress. Recently it’s been enough keep me from getting in my car and going to the casino, and that gives me hope that I haven’t felt in a long time. Highly recommended for anyone that struggles with the addiction cycle and isn’t quite sure how to break it.

title: Awesome App
body:
04/12/2023 Update: I think it would be helpful to add a brief notes section too.  For example, if I’m fasting from specific foods & drinks, I might want to add a note in the notes section the brief foods & drinks I’m fasting from.  I think that would be helpful.

Just downloaded a few seconds ago and this is exactly the app I’m looking for. User interface is pleasant to view and very easy to use. I am able to quickly access the data im looking for.  I also like the colors and font being used. 

 I do however have one suggestion and that is to add a temporary “stop counter” button. Why? Because if I fail during one of my challenges, I may binge out multiple times in one day before getting back on track. I don’t want to keep resetting the counter. I also don’t want to delete the counter because it appears that will delete my streaks. I definitely don’t want to delete my steaks. 

 For example, if I fail during a fast food challenge, I may binge and eat two more fast food meals in a day before getting back on track to eating no more fast food. I wouldn’t want to keep resetting the counter after each fast food meal, I would rather pause the counter temporarily and then restart the counter after I feel I’m ready to start my fast food challenge again (while still keeping my previous streaks). Other than that awesome app. I already highly recommend.

title: Beautiful App that Could Be Much More
body:
I’ve been looking everywhere for a tally/time since/time until app, and have hit many roadblocks. Habit trackers aren’t very helpful, as they attach positive/negative significance to each repetition when I’d like a neutral log. Other features I’m looking for include time tracking down to the second (which this app has), notes attached to entries, and statistics/charting ability.
Days Since is beautiful. I love the calendar view, it’s not buggy, the colors are enough to keep it from looking dull without being overpowering, there are options for Face ID and importing/exporting options. The only problem is that it’s not what I need, as what I’m tracking isn’t sobriety or bad habits. 
I understand that the developer wasn’t designing this app for me or to be used for my purposes (hence the enthusiastic five stars), but I’d love to see an app with the features I’m seeking based on this one - it has enormous potential.

title: Yes, you need this app.
body:
Need to break a habit? Get this app right now! (I sound like a bot) I don’t know how but somehow seeing how long it’s been since you’ve fed a bad habit helps me quit it! There are a couple of tiny pet peeves I have that I’d like to address though…

Developers, please consider:

1. You can’t rearrange your counters in the main menu, where you see all your counters

— While yes, you can rearrange them through another button, I just thought it would be nice if it was easier. Think Siri Shortcuts, the menu looks similar to that and you can easily rearrange the shortcuts.

2. Tapping a counter brings up a menu, it doesn’t reset it

— Again, think Siri Shortcuts. Tap a shortcut to run it, and tap a small button on the right to access and edit the shortcut. If the devs wanted it to be cleaner, you could put an edit button on the top left to replace the rearranging menu. Clicking it would make the counters start to jiggle (like Jiggle Mode) then tapping on the corresponding counter would let you edit its info.

3. You can’t edit the time of previous resets

— This is self-explanatory. If the devs ever read this, please add this. (There is a high possibility that this is a pro feature and I’m just as dense as a rock)

Thanks, Days Since team! 

I look forward to seeing Days Since as well as my physical and mental well-being progress!

title: Great App to curb OCD compulsions

When people out of my personal circle began noticing, I became frantic in my search to have better sleep and clearer skin. Upon coming across Days Since I realized immediately that this app has great potential for habit management with the streak counters. I get really hooked to the streak counters as I almost have a 2 year streak in Duolingo, which has been helping me learn French without breaks in between. I cannot state enough how much this app has changed my life and I feel confident like never before when among society. I highly recommend this app to anyone who has trouble with their erratic habits or whoever wants to lead a drug free, tobacco, and alcohol free life. It is great for practically anything and is fully customizable.

title: Simple, yet Powerful.
body:
I am surprised how much I love this app. I started by doing the usual things. I plugged in the date when I quit smoking and when I went vegan. Very interesting to see how much time elapsed. I love playing with color options and formats… you can view the length of elapsed time in different ways, like days, months, and years. 

I love the reset function as well. If you need to reset you just tap the button and it restarts the count. 

Where I really was surprised is how often I use it. I recently had eye surgery and logged it in. My doctor asked how long it was since my surgery I was able to tell him to the minute lol. We were monitoring how long I had the gas bubble visible in my eye. 

I love this app for everything it does. Seriously. It’s simple, clean, elegant and it works flawlessly. 

Let’s support our Indie developers! Job well done.

title: No more questions on “how long have you been together?”
body:
I was tired. I couldn’t help it any longer. I knew the dates, each one of them. When we met, the year we started dating for real, when did we move in together, the wedding… But I couldn’t keep track of doing the math each time anyone asked “how long have you been together?”
Days Since helped me put an end on this debate. Now I just can open the app and check it out: this many years we’ve known each other, that much years dating, a long time living together, X years of marriage. 
Bonus: I can also track when I started doing something good for myself (such as regular exercise) and how long have I stopped a bad habit. It has been fun, thanks developers for this very easy to use and awesome app.

title: Genuine dev team
body:
First off, the development team seems genuine and true to their word that they are here to help. If you look at other apps on the AppStore a lot of them seem like they want to help but money is definitely a driving factor for them. The fact that this team gives you a week trial and tells you to set a calendar reminder to cancel so you won’t be charged is huge. The app is about $20 a year after the trial which to me I usually wouldn’t consider paying. Due to the genuine attitude this team is portraying I have absolutely no problem paying. They don’t sell your data and what they keep is anonymized according to their privacy policy. The app is simple, looks good, and is straight to the point.

One feature that this app lacks that I would love to see is the ability to edit a note after resetting a timer. I often reset the timer with a note, and reset it again after vaping with a new note on how I feel about what I just did or how my day was going etc. I would like to edit the note so I can do this without impacting the timer.

Other than that missing feature, this app is great and I love the widget. Keep up the work, I and I’m sure many others appreciate what you are doing to help us manage this addiction.

title: Admittedly, I only use this app for a joke

Myself, being an insensitive ~jokester,~ downloaded this app because I needed something to track the days since “they thought it was safe to eat.” My friend is kind of a dunce who doesn’t pay attention to what food they put in their face and, as such, make mistakes when judging the safety of their meals and make themselves sick. This happens every few weeks or so. Hence the day counter. It works well for what it is, and I’m sure that people who need more serious trackers (or light-hearted ones) would find this absolutely acceptable. I do wish that it wouldn’t ask me for the premium version so much, but I understand revenue is revenue and I’m not gonna begrudge you guys for asking for money. I only need the app for a joke so I don’t foresee myself paying, but I don’t think that the free version is in any way lacking. Overall, it works great and my friend and I enjoy the joke.

title: This app is great! Helps you discipline yourself by holding you accountable
body:
Been using it to years to tack my abstinence streak of various things i decided were no good for me (ex: alcohol, soda, red meat/poultry, pornography, vaping). I use it help myself practice temperance/moderation in other areas of my life (ex: eating out, staying up late, using NRT products). I also use it just to encourage myself to better myself in general (ex: days since I’ve skipped exercising, days since I’ve had an argument/confrontation with someone). Love seeing the amount of years/months/days/hours go up little by little until the number is huger than I ever thought possible— very rewarding feeling! In areas of life I practice temperance/moderation instead of abstinence and in areas of life I’m just trying to better myself it’s still encouraging to see my “longest steak” & “average streak” increase slowly overtime—it prevents me from feeling guilty or ashamed when I “lapse” and have to reset the counter because I focus on my streak instead of the fact that I lapsed/failed. Sometimes I feel a tiny but noticeable amount of disappointment and/or frustration when i lapse and have to reset the counter (no guilt or shame though so it’s fine) but I think that’s normal because it just remotivates me to discipline myself more so I can improve my steak in the future. Very good for learning self discipline and holding yourself accountable for your actions. Highly recommend if you have a personality like mine!

Only features I would like to have: 1)More decorative colors for the counters. I wish all of mine could be different. 2) An option to display the way your streak is displayed when you tap on “year”. For example my counter for “Red Meat” shows as “3 years | 8 months | 16 days | 16 hours” because of the way I’m naturally inclined to count time in my head I wish I had the option to display it as “3 years | 8 months | 2 weeks | 2.5 days”

I definitely recommend to anyone trying to quit a bad habit!

title: extremely helpful app!
body:
since i started using this app i’ve noticed how much improvement i’ve made. i know a lot of people say not to track things since it seems to hyper-fixate your mind on your habits/addictions, but this the way that i see it:

once you spend time and effort into doing (or in this sense, not doing) something and see the progress of how long you’ve been doing that for, it makes you value your effort more.

think of it like a snapchat streak. nobody really cares about what snaps you send anymore after the first few weeks, but what matters is the time and energy you’ve invested into doing something for so long that in your brain you grow to care for it and wouldn’t do anything to ruin it. it’s a motivation.

since i started using this app i’d constantly be attentive every day of how many hours i’d gone without indulging in bad habits, but slowly it slipped my mind. i stopped checking the days and even thinking about it in the first place. yes i had cravings but looking at that effort i put in made me see the clear picture. every now and then i check it just to give myself a confidence boost, or a mental reward i should say. i highly, HIGHLY recommend this app to anyone who has trouble detaching from habits.

title: Simple, Aesthetic, and Functional!
body: It's exactly what I was looking for! A simple way to track my streaks. I love this, since it makes it so much easier for me to quit things when I can *visually* see with my eyes I've been clean for weeks or months and I realize just how far I've come. This app couldn't have made it easier. It's extremely simple, you just create a streak with the “+” button and reset it with a button when you relapse. I bet your GRANDMA could use this app to overcome her crippling crack cocaine addiction! On top of this, it's aesthetically a very pretty app. I love the minimalistic approach the creators took, just like you'd expect for such a simple and easy to use app like this. Most importantly out of everything though, this app does it's job flawlessly. I haven't encountered a single issue yet! It's got widget implementation, a very fairly and cheaply priced premium version (which isn't anywhere near necessary to have in order to use the app), and finally a very nice locking feature (via face ID or passcode) so no one but you can access the app if you need to keep people out. Also many more features, those are just my favorites. FR though, what are you doing? Download this app already and see for yourself! I love this app, thank you! :D

title: I do love this app. 5-stars for one additional feature
body: I do love this app. Especially the ability to reset a streak. This creates a nice history log. For example, if you quit smoking for 5 days, had a cigarette, then reset, over time you can see the history of streaks/attempts. The one thing that would make this really nice is when upon resetting a streak, you could have the ability to “pause”, so another streak wouldn’t automatically start. Taking the smoking example, if a person quit smoking for 20 days, then started smoking and didn’t quit again until 10 days later, they could reset their streak, when they started to smoke, pause the streak, and then when they try quitting again, in this case 10 days later, they could start the streak up again. Other than that, I really like this app. To have that additional feature would just turn it from a 4-star review to a 5- star review. And it doesn’t seem like it would be that hard to implement so get on it!!! :-)

title: Appreciate it, would like to suggest more.
body: I’m satisfied with the simplicity of this app. I’m currently using it for a sobriety counter, and would like to suggest some features that could potentially be helpful. I also understand if these suggestions are not the direction you’re going for, as I can tell by the design it’s more to be used as a simple counter/tool. Anyway, the first suggestion I had was any sort of notification-specific rewards or reminders. Something like “your ___ counter has reached ___ days, congrats!” And maybe having an option to select from a negative, neutral, or positive message or set to none/no notifications. These can be counter specific as well. (Hypothetically). My next suggestion was a “stop counting” option, like if you no longer want to count it after a certain amount of days, and then maybe a notification that was like “your ____ counter stopped, check it out!” (I don’t know) Or a way to make it so that certain lack of use doesn’t count towards your overall progress statistics—sometimes I forget to track or have something else going on that day and don’t want my lack of counting to affect the statistics of the progress I’ve made. I can probably think of more but at the moment I’m stumped and should be getting some sleep. So goodnight and thank you for this great app.

title: Days since is great!!!
body: This app is truly amazing. It's unbelievable how much easier this makes it to harness my willpower for my own personal growth. I am not giving a full five stars however because I see some fairly simple ways in which this app's effectiveness could be even further increased. There should be a "points system" where you can see your "current days since score", which is the number of days of all of your current active streaks added up. If this were combined with a simple points over time line graph visualization, users would be further incentivized to continue their streaks. Additionally, you could add in simple "sticker" type graphical award incentives (like snapchat streak emojis) to further increase the apps effectiveness. Keep up the great work and please implement these things!!

title: Really Amazing App!!!
body: I’ve had a few bad habits that I have managed to quit using this app. I’ve said goodbye to junk food, too much inactivity, and smoking. I’ve also been spending significantly less time on my phone these days. Now I just say, like probably many people, I had reached a crossroads. So as to say, once I dropped all my bad habits successfully, it felt as if there was nothing special about it other than knowing I’m on a road to better health. For anyone who may be struggling with that, there’s a few things I’ve learned and gained in addition from just reflecting on myself and my past bad habits. Removing bad habits (addictions) allows you to live in the present moment. Admittedly, this was very scary at first. You become highly aware of your own mortality. I have learned to embrace it though and I am working on building productive habits to replace the bad habits. So my advice to you is to work on replacing the bad habits with healthy and productive habits. Because if not then you will be left with a void. You’re going to feel this emptiness. This sense of losing purpose. Keep in mind that bad habits you used to do constantly kept your mind distracted and running from traumas and such. It’s a good opportunity to face all of your traumas head on and let go of everything bad. It will be easier than you think. Don’t question the process. Just trust it.

title: This One
body:
Simple and easy to use interface, understated graphics, robust reliability, and (a rarity these days) as good as it gets privacy protection!!!  Always investigate that for any app.  After trying other apps, this is the one I’m keeping.  (re: Version 1.16.8 June, 2022)

I'm using this as a general purpose days-since counter (rather than for behavior modification… although I probably should!) and for general use I have 3 suggestions:

1)It would be more accommodating of a larger number of entries (and possibly users) by allowing an option to display counters in single, stacked, horizontal lines for less scrolling.  But as is works great to emphasize the importance and separateness of each entry.

2)It might be helpful to also have options to automatically sort entries by most days since, and to reverse that sort.

3)Add the ability to group sub entries under a common subject.

Nice work!

title: Very Useful, But Better With a Few Tweaks:
body:
This app is great. It tracks your progress and doesn’t judge you for resetting a counter should you give in to whatever reason you set it for. The calendar view is a great tangible way to see how you do throughout each month, and I even use it to keep accountability with a friend so they can keep tabs on my own progress. Tracking how long on average you go before a reset and what your longest period between resets was is also a great way to judge your progress and mark your own milestones. For any of you looking to try a nice and simple solution to break some bad habits, give this one a shot. It’s free, and is very intuitive to use, granted that you keep up with your own progress and document each time you need to reset a counter. 

One thing I’d really like though is this: you already allow the removal of resets if you tap the edit button when searching through resets on a given counter. It would be awesome if you were able to edit the comment or time there as well, just so you wouldn’t have to delete and redo the reset if you realize you forgot to document something or put AM instead of PM or something like that. Other than that, I really can’t complain, but that tiny missing feature has bugged me for a while, so I thought I’d write a review and mention it. Other than that, this app is extremely simple and could use a bit of polish here and there. Things like milestone markers for longest streak on the calendar itself could be large incentives for lasting longer without a reset. Perhaps even milestones for increasing the average time between resets could encourage further control over bad habits. Just a few ideas for the future if you are so inclined. ;) Thanks for reading!

title: Keeps me on track
body: I like this App. I can set more than one category and when I open the app the info is all on one page. For me it’s motivating to look at how long I’ve been working towards a goal.  I set two goals for myself 1)Days without refined sugar and 2) Days without alcoholic beverages. Neither of these goals was set out of a critical need but more of a personal desire to achieve better overall health. Last night we had a dinner party and we were serving cocktails and I briefly thought, I’ll just have one drink with everyone else, but I opened the app and saw that it had been 16 days since I last had a beverage and I really didn’t want to hit restart on that counter! So I passed on the beverages and woke up feeling great today and proud that I stuck with my decision to continue on a healthy path. However, I did eat a couple of Oreos and had to reset my refined sugar counter to 0. This is a great tool to track progress and can be a great motivator for people who like to set personal goals.

title: A fairly good app
body: There’s nothing special about this app. This app was alright, though. All that it really does is allows you to set a habit tracker and you make sure that you don’t do it again. I have three bad habits that I need to break, but again this app is pretty normal and it helps to remind me that I need to quit. It also helps with being able to see how many days I’ve gone without doing it again because it encourages and motivates me to keep going. Although, once I really do quit my habit what else is there to do? There is no flair or anything super special they happens if I did hit a one year milestone. I like that you can reset the counter, but I want to know, developer, where is the pizzazz that I’m looking for or a little something to keep me motivated. What if those numbers aren’t enough? This is what I would like to see as an improvement to this app. Push notifications. With these enabled, you can see motivating quotes or a little sentence to remind you that you’re doing a great job. I feel that this can also be done in the app itself so that you can also view inspiring reminders if you keep visiting the app to see your progress. I know that there can be many more visual pleasing updates that can be added to this app but definitely keep my advice in mind. Thank you for your time.

If you are looking for a way to keep you accountable for your habits, this might be a good options. At least it was for me, as I am always using my phone during the day. It is easy for me to see that  widget every time I open my main screen. title: Very helpful.
body: I’ve been on the mission to stop smoking for some time now. I always thought it would be impossible because for me I get that urge to smoke when I don’t have it. This was always why I’m past times I would say “I could never stop” but by the Grace of My Lord and Savior Jesus I’ve been able to overcome so much more than I thought I would. I got a Bible and started reading and when I would read the Bible on those days I wouldn’t have as many urges. Crazy to think that reading a book could feminism physical addiction urges right? The app was a great way for me to keep track of my progress to remind myself if I ever do get an urge or an apatite for smoking. I still do get urges occasionally if I havnt been reading my Bible but that’s why I love the app so much. It gives me motivation and it gives me something to physically see. If you do mess up there’s no shame because you can reset that timer and your back at it again. You can make different timers for different things too maybe you vape also or maybe you smoke weed or something. You can set different timers for all the things you need to tackle no matter what it is so I think the app is great and I’m really appreciative of it!

title: Great Motivation for Both Healthy/Unhealthy Habits
body:
This app is so helpful of keeping track of how long I’ve made it since I’ve kicked some nasty habits (vaping, binge eating, and consuming alcohol). It’s so motivating to see how far I’ve come, and when I’m thinking of relapse, just looking at this counter makes me not want to break my streak. 

You can also use it for positive reminders, like days since you had a baby or a new pet, so you can celebrate those mini milestones. Or days since you’ve picked up a healthy habit, like eating a balanced diet, started a fitness routine, started a new job, the possibilities are endless. 

Overall, a great app. The only thing I would like to see in the future is possibly allowing reminders to check in. Not every day, but I’ll admit, once or twice I should have reset my counter and forgot. It’s a problem with myself though, and perhaps others prefer to not receive notifications.

Now that I’m in a spot that I have been clean for a while, you can’t help but to get an itch to be crazy sometimes. title: Maybe it’s simple enough to work?
body:
I gave it three stars because I don’t like that the only way to really hold yourself accountable is to post it on social media (they gave that as an option in the app). I would prefer other features, A different kind of reward system. Or even just a simple reminder to look at my progress throughout the day or the week or whatever. Right now it’s pretty cool but I’m worried I’m going to forget about the app and it’s going to get lost in my homepage. Other than that, I think basic premise is pretty cool. It just needs some really simple additions, like a notification system 

edit: I updated my review from three stars to four. It’s actually working better than I thought it would. I still wish there was some type of notification or reminder to check it. Very simple counter system without a lot of bells and whistles. I am six days into no smoking . If I make it to 30, I’ll update it to five stars

title: Help me break a bad habit fast
body:
I was trying to stop drinking alcohol and I struggled to stay consistent. This app has been the best tool yet. Even better than the other apps aimed at breaking addiction. I like how you can track in hours, days, weeks, etc. I moved from hours to days and then to weeks as time went on and it gave me a fresh look. The only things I would add to the app is the ability to edit the date. I found this app a few days into my fast and I wish I could edit the date to reflect the actual start date instead of the date I found the app. I just had to always add 3 days to the app’s date. Note to developers!! 

Thanks for this tool!! It is great!

title: Best AD-FREE counter app out there!
body:
Let me just start off by saying, I really adore this app! It’s so functional, simple, and aesthetically clean. It’s great to see an app that’s actually designed for its practicality and for its users! If you are looking for a app to count how many days it’s been, all the way down to the second, this is the perfect app! I really cannot recommend it enough!

Pros
NO ADS! (Astonishing, I know)
Simple to use
Great design
Very clear interface

And for the developers I have only one small complaint about the app, the lack of color choices for the counters. If it were at all possible (I don’t know how difficult coding is) I believe that adding a color wheel to the color options would be a great feature. Having only 15 color choices does make things very simple, but also limits users. Of course it’s not the end of the world if that’s not doable but that is the only complaint I have! Thank you for the small indie team that makes this wonderful app that helps tons of people :)

title: Trackable self-accountability
body:
I’ve been using this app to try and focus on daily habits that I’m usually not very good at. I use it to make sure that I’ve taken care of myself in a way that’s difficult for a sprint of days, and the fact that it tracks resets is a gentle encouragement and a useful type of accountability.

I keep a useful widget on my home screen that shows how many days it’s been since I’ve had alcohol, and how many days it’s been since I made another large change in my life that has been positive. It’s minimal and non-intrusive and not pushy. No reminders that shame you if you’ve had to reset no notifications to tell you that you need to check it, it’s incredibly passive if you don’t deal well with pressure. It just reminds you how long you’ve been doing a thing and how many times you’ve failed at sticking to that routine. That little bit of accountability has really changed my perspective

This has become a vital part of my self-care routine and I really really appreciate how simple and useful this app is.

title: Works Perfect For My Needs
body: App is free and does everything I need it to do. Actually it does a little more than I need as well because it also keeps track of things other than just how many hours/days/weeks/months/years (and yes you can easily switch between those time units to see how long it’s been) but also see things like your longest time without, your average time without, and how long you’ve been keeping such a counter. It’s also nice that it lets you rename your counters whatever you’d like. I’d rather not have the direct words for what I’m keeping track of on the counter, so I often write abbreviations and I know what it means. You can also change the colors of the counters and thats fun. Ive had this app for a little over a year and I’d definitely recommend it to anyone needing to keep track of days since, for which the app is named promptly. I’m probably forgetting some other features just because I’ve had it so long and Im used to them, but absolutely its a wonderful app. I’ve also never encountered an ad, or needed to pay for something to unlock special features, which is really nice considering that when I have to reset my counters I’m not in a good mental state so having to wait for ads and be bombarded by other content would be overwhelming and frustrating. Honestly I’ve never encountered anything on it that I think would need fixing, as “too good to be true” as that sounds, it really is just an app made incredibly well. Overall an excellent app that does everything I need and more; it’s designed really well both in terms of function and aesthetic. Easily navigated and takes next to no time to learn how to use. Would 100% recommend to anyone looking to keep track of days since any habit.
